KXNCAAF1H-26NOV11BUFFBALL.rules_primary_example: If Ball St. wins the 1st half of the Buffalo vs Ball St. college football game originally scheduled for Nov 11, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
KXNCAAF1H-26NOV11BUFFBALL.rules_secondary: Note: Only points scored during the 1st half of play count towards this market. If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result. If the game is not started within 48 hours, the market will resolve to a fair price.
settlement_sources: Kalshi using information originating from the NCAA

first_half_moneyline.estimate: P(team leads at halftime) / P(tie at halftime)
gaps: team first-half splits are raw and unadjusted (football.period_splits_raw)
first_half_moneyline.note: first-half history is conditional on the full-game baseline; team first-half scoring splits are raw (unadjusted) and opening scripts are not captured, so early-game tendencies come from those splits plus early-down success rate and neutral pass rate.

game_moneyline.note: likely winner, realistic upset pathways: use the dominant / competitive / upset script set in `game_script`.

game_spread.estimate: P(team wins by more than the line)
game_spread.note: expected margin, control, mismatch and backdoor-cover risk (the margin distribution's width is the backdoor risk). Spread rungs are one ladder: P is monotone in the line.

game_total.note: projected possessions x scoring efficiency, explosive plays, defensive matchups; weather and tempo shift the whole ladder.

inputs: football.matchup (that team's offense vs the actual opposing defense)
team_total.note: price a team total from THAT offense versus THIS defense, not from the game total split evenly.

price_provenance.captured_at_meaning: the last time the market content CHANGED, not the last time the collector observed it. The workflow does not commit an unchanged surface.
price_provenance.rule: every price below is a capture from the catalog collector, not a live order-book quote. Compare `game_fingerprint` with `data/live/execution/games/<game_key>/quotes.json`: if they differ, the quotes file is newer and wins. Confirm any price on Kalshi before acting.

pricing_basis.all_in_per_contract: ask + the ORDER's taker fee / contracts, for a one-unit order; fee = ceil_to_cent(multiplier x 0.07 x contracts x P x (1-P))
pricing_basis.break_even_probability: equals all_in: the probability that the side you BUY wins at which expected value is zero
pricing_basis.buy_NO: pay no_ask (= 1 - yes_bid, NEVER 1 - yes_ask); size is no.ask_size (the YES bid book)

contract_fields.ref_freq: share of n comparable past games in which the YES outcome occurred: descriptive reference class, NOT a fair probability
contract_fields.upd: when Kalshi last changed the contract; a thin ladder rung can be days old
contract_fields.yes/no.all_in: ask + one-unit order fee spread over its contracts = break-even probability for that side
contract_fields.yes/no.ask: price to BUY that side (NO uses the NO ask)
contract_fields.yes/no.ask_size: contracts quoted at that ask at capture (NO size is the YES bid book)
contract_fields.yes/no.exec: positive quoted size on that side at capture (NOT live-verified)

side_teams.rule: `side` on a contract is the FOOTBALL game's home/away (matches football.* in packet.json); verify the code-to-team pairing here
